Subject: 40 hours of light. 95 grams. Meet the Beacon.
Preview: A headlamp built for the long nights you actually plan for.
Body: You know the drill: headlamp dies at mile 18, or you're rationing battery life through a three-day route because you didn't want to carry the heavier one.

The Beacon is designed around that specific frustration.

400 lumens gives you enough light to move confidently on trail or read a map in a crowded tent. The runtime is 40 hours on a single charge — enough for a long weekend without nursing the battery. When you do need to top it off, it charges via USB-C, the same cable you're likely already carrying.

It weighs 95 grams. Not ultralight-obsession territory, but light enough that it disappears into your kit.

The Beacon is a solid three-season headlamp for hiking, camping, and around-camp work. It isn't designed for technical caving, extreme cold, or submersion.

No frills. Just a well-built light that shows up when you need it.
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
